summary: Hamma Hamma Guard Station, a CCC cabin of 1936-37 planned as a guard station and lookout, still stands and is rented by the Forest Service.

facts.design: Combined guard station and fire lookout cabin with an observation room; built by the CCC in 1936-37

access.note: Rented as a cabin through Recreation.gov; short gated road, with gate access given to guests

visit.trail_note: Short gated road leads to the cabin. From Hoodsport, Highway 101 north 14 miles to Hamma Hamma River Road, then 5.7 miles to the access road.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Olympic National Forest

events.note: Planning for a combined Forest Guard Station and Lookout; a May 1936 letter describes the area as blind
CCC construction, 1936-1937 per Campflare; completed in 1937 per Revisiting Washington

evidence.supports: Listed by the FFLA as a standing ground site in Mason County
evidence.quote: Hamma Hamma GS Mason 47.59248 -123.11509 Ground Standing

evidence.supports: Planned in 1936 as a combined guard station and lookout
evidence.quote: In 1936, plans were being made to build a combined Forest Guard Station and Lookout.

evidence.supports: Guard station sits on a bench overlooking the valley
evidence.quote: the guard station was located on a bench overlooking the territory several miles up and down the valley.

evidence.supports: A May 1936 letter described the area as blind; the proposed design pushed the living room out for window space
evidence.quote: The letter described the area as BLIND, so the proposed design on the building projected the living room out toward the brow of the bench to provide visibility with the increased window space.

evidence.supports: Built 1936-1937 by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: Built from 1936-1937 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, this former Forest Service guard station is nominated to the National Register of Historic Places for its skilled craftsmanship.
The CCC-constructed Guard Station, completed in 1937, is available for rent year-round.

evidence.supports: Gate below the station was to restrict the watershed in fire season, per the 1936 plan
evidence.quote: the Hamma Hamma watershed would be restricted during fire season by a gate below the guard station.

evidence.supports: Guard had to leave patrol to unlock the gate; the document says this cost detection time, for anyone holding a permit
evidence.quote: the guard would have to leave his patrol duty and go down to unlock the gate

evidence.supports: Building still standing and rented as a Forest Service vacation rental
evidence.quote: The Guard Station is still standing today and is used as a vacation rental by the Forest Service.

evidence.supports: Nominated to the National Register of Historic Places (per Campflare only)
evidence.quote: nominated to the National Register of Historic Places for its skilled craftsmanship.

evidence.supports: Booked via Recreation.gov; open year-round; closed Thursdays; seven-night maximum
evidence.quote: Open year-round. Closed Thursdays for cleaning. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is seven consecutive nights.

evidence.supports: Short gated road; guests given gate access, gate may or may not be open
evidence.quote: A short gated road leads up to the structure, guests are given the gate access so it may or may not be open.

evidence.supports: No potable water on site; guests bring their own
evidence.quote: there is no potable water on-site; guests must bring their own drinking and cooking water.

evidence.supports: Directions: Highway 101 north 14 miles to Hamma Hamma River Road
evidence.quote: From Hoodsport, WA take Highway 101 north for 14 miles to Hamma Hamma River Road.

evidence.supports: Directions: 5.7 miles on Hamma Hamma River Road to the access road
evidence.quote: travel 5.7 miles to the access road to the cabin.

evidence.supports: Forest Service describes one historic cabin in the Hamma Hamma drainage

notes_for_editor: The site is a combined guard station and lookout cabin, not a tower; the record's kind 'ground' fits the vocabulary. Standing status and the rental are supported by WillhiteWeb (undated) and Campflare. No staffing history and no fire history were found in the pages read, so staffing is left out. The NRHP nomination rests on Campflare alone and no listing was confirmed. The WillhiteWeb page gives elevation as 600 feet (about 183 m), which the record lacks (elevation_m is null). The cached firelookout.com Washington page is only 590 characters and has no Hamma Hamma line, so it does not settle the FFLA conflict. A search summary mentioned fire spotting use and a July 2025 fire in the drainage; neither was verified on a page and neither is in the story. Campflare's trail length (quarter-mile) conflicts with a search snippet (1.5 miles), so the trail length is left out.
